newsitem.title: UK: Ldn freight - Firmer fixtures buoy owners.
newsitem.headline: Ldn freight - Firmer fixtures buoy owners.

text.p: The Baltic Freight Index bounded higher by 23 points to 1,118 on Thursday and shipbrokers said the market buzzed with talk of fixtures at substantially higher levels for Panamaxes and Handy-sizes in the North Atlantic.

The BFI's jump was no surprise to owners and charterers operating in this theatre. Grain charterers were largely responsible for the firmer conditions although Far Eastern charterers contributed to the generally more optimistic scene for owners by concluding a number of Panamax fixtures on period timecharter.
Brokers considered that Capers appeared to be in stronger demand in the East where a possible slight improvement for Handy-sizes was also noted.

A large number of Panamax vessels were fixed on subjects for US Gulf business although the exact rates were sometimes disputed. The 1985-built Marifran-relet North Duchess 63,785 dwt was reported booked delivery rotterdam about Oct 25 for a trip via US Gulf to the Far East by Hanjin at a very firm $10,500 daily, but others believed the rate was $10,500 daily basis US Gulf plus $190,000 bonus. The 1980-built Poros 62,135 dwt was also rumoured to have been taken by Hanjin on subjects in the same trade at $10,000 daily plus unknown bonus - others pitched the rate higher at $10,500 daily plus $175,000 bonus.

Maritime Nancy 71,733 dwt having been fixed for 12 months at about $9,250/9,500 daily was believed relet delivery prompt Continent for a trip via US Gulf to the Far East at $10,500 daily. More interesting rumours suggested that Heraklia 65,159 dwt in ballast from the Pacific fixed delivery US Gulf early Nov trip Far East at $11,000 daily plus $200,000 bonus and that a modern 73,000 dwt vessel was fixed on this route delivery Oct/Nov at up to $12,000 daily plus the same bonus. Meanwhile it was understood that Cargill were still quoting their early Nov HSS Panamax order for US Gulf/Continent at $10.00 and only seeing tonnage Aski over $12.00. 54,000 HSS US Gulf/Japan for Nov 15/30 was rumoured fixed at $22.00 no combo, up $1.50 from Hanjin's fixture for similar dates earlier this week.

Also, $22.00 is said to have been bid for US Gulf/China for early Nov, but Andre quote only $21.00 for 50,000/10 US Gulf/China for Oct/Nov. Cho Yang were linked with Bontrader 59,662 dwt on subjects for US Gulf/S Korea. Egyptian charterers were believed to have fixed 2 Panamaxes with grain from the Continent but full details were not avaable. In the East Halla were said to have covered 4 Panamaxes for Pacific rounds - Maratha Messenger and Dimitris A as reported, as well as Alam Baru 65,117 dwt delivery prompt Kinuura at a firm $8,200 daily and possibly Atlantic Savior 64,000 dwt on subjects. There are reports that Sinochart fixed Nephele 71,930 dwt delivery China end Oct for 3-5 months at $7,900 daily but these could not be confirmed.

In parallel with the Panamaxes Handy rates are being pushed up sharply in the Atlantic, mainly because of strong demand in the US Gulf. An over-age Fortune type of 22,000 dwt was bid well over $5,000 daily delivery Continent for a TransAtlantic grain round voyage. Charterers with 25,000 HSS US Gulf/Morocco were said to be quoting $14.00 against owners at over $19.00 and 25,000 HSS US Gulf/Aqaba at $23.50 against $29.00.

Brokers suggested that Capers were enjoying stronger demand in the East and that a number of private fixtures in the coal and ore trades had been concluded in the Atlantic. Medmar fixed about 95,000 ironore Tubarao/Misurata for mid-Nov on private terms. Vessels have been taken from various other loading areas in substitute for Narvik. Cargill covered a Panamax cargo of fertilizers Tampa/China on private terms.

Darya Ma 30,750 dwt has been fixed delivery Sweden trip East Med at $7,400 daily and Albatross may have booked Pacific Prince 42,000 dwt delivery Norway trip Far East at close to $11,250 daily. Bron are understood to have taken Ayane 27,082 dwt for a Lakes round on private terms. Although conditions may be improving in the Far East Wadi al Kamar 45,000 dwt went to Yukong delivery Port Hedland trip S Korea at only $7,500 daily plus $65,000 bonus. World Umpire 47,000 dwt has been fixed on subjects.
